It stays inconclusive only because the supporting check fails: the upper |forecast| half earns 0.11 % less short excess than the lower half. My quartiles of the cases show no grading either: 0.97 % (t 1.66), 0.00 %, 0.66 %, 0.20 % from smallest to largest |forecast|.
findings.F2: The forecast multiplies two parts that grade in opposite directions. The weekend's fall size grades against continuation:
findings.F3: The other part, the weekend's hourly volatility against the prior week, grades the way the idea predicts:
findings.F4: The vol-ratio grading holds in both halves of the data, with the top-quartile short excess at +0.91 % (t 1.28) in 2018–2021 and +1.64 % (t 2.35) in 2022–2025. It is positive in all six coins (0.29 % for ZEC to 2.10 % for XRP). It is not stable by year: 2019 −0.54 %, 2020 −0.35 % and 2025 −1.56 % against 2022 +4.14 % and 2024 +3.76 % (t 4.73).

findings.F6: The 48-hour horizon is where the effect shows. On the cases, the short excess is 0.09 % (t 0.39) at 24 hours, 0.46 % (t 1.51) at 48 hours and 0.36 % (t 0.94) at 72 hours. The plan's own size, an unusual move of 0.68 % per case, is 3.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: When a coin falls over the weekend (Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC), it keeps falling over Monday and Tuesday. The fall is larger the more volatile the weekend's hours were compared with the coin's previous week, graded by that volatility comparison alone and not by the size of the weekend's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to buy a weekend dip the more turbulent the weekend's hourly trading was against the prior week, and may lean short for the next two days in proportion to that turbulence.
ideas.name: turbulent weekend falls continue

ideas.idea: When a coin's hourly moves over the weekend (Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC) were more volatile than over its previous week, the coin keeps moving in the direction of its weekend return over the next 2 days. The continuation is larger the higher the weekend's volatility compared with the previous week.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to fade a weekend move made on turbulent trading, and may follow its direction over Monday and Tuesday, more so the more turbulent the weekend was.
ideas.name: turbulent weekends keep their direction
